headline: Carbon is the backbone of all life—the single element that makes biology possible
universal_truth: Versatility is power; the ability to connect in many ways creates endless possibilities
fun_facts: Carbon can form more compounds than all other elements combined
The carbon in your body was once inside a star, then perhaps in a dinosaur, then in the air
Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon—same element, radically different structure
discussion_questions: How does knowing you're made of ancient stardust change your self-perception?
What makes something versatile—able to work in many different contexts?
What's your 'carbon'—the quality that lets you connect and adapt?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every living thing on Earth—every plant, animal, bacterium, and you—is built on carbon. This single element forms the backbone of DNA, proteins, fats, and carbohydrates. Life is carbon-based. No carbon, no life as we know it.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: There are over 100 elements, but life chose carbon as its foundation. Why? What makes carbon special enough to be the universal building block of all living things?
cliff.prompt: Why is carbon the basis of life?

options.text: Carbon can form four bonds, creating complex chains and structures
options.response: Yes. Carbon's ability to bond in four directions lets it build infinitely complex molecules.

options.text: Carbon is the most abundant element on Earth
options.response: Carbon is common, but its chemistry is what matters...

q1.title: The Connector
q1.script: Carbon can form four chemical bonds—more than almost any element. It can bond to itself in long chains, rings, and branches. This creates millions of possible molecules. Carbon's superpower is versatility.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Connector"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Ancient Atoms
q2.script: The carbon in your body has been recycling through Earth's systems for billions of years. It was forged in stars, drifted through space, became part of ancient seas and creatures. Some carbon atoms in you may have been in dinosaurs, in Caesar, in countless others.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Structure Matters
q3.script: Diamond is the hardest natural material. Graphite is soft enough for pencils. Both are pure carbon—the difference is structure. Same atoms, arranged differently, create completely different properties. How things connect matters as much as what connects.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Versatility is power. Carbon teaches that the ability to connect in many ways—to form diverse bonds and structures—creates infinite possibilities. Cultivate your ability to connect diversely.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 73. Tomorrow, we'll explore the gas you don't notice—nitrogen. Until then, marvel that you're made of stardust, recycled through billions of years.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Connection Diversity - Build More Bonds
growTrack.activity: Carbon's power is forming diverse bonds. Where in your life could you connect more diversely—new types of relationships, skills, or experiences? Identify one new type of connection you could cultivate this month.
